The peace lily is thirsty: it has gone without water long enough that the soil is dry and the leaves are drooping, which is the plant's way of conserving moisture. [keyword: water]
Overwatering in a pot without drainage is keeping the soil waterlogged, causing the lower leaves to yellow from root stress. [keyword: overwater]
The jade plant is not getting enough light, which causes etiolation: long, stretched stems and small, pale new leaves as it reaches for light. [keyword: light]
The brown, crispy frond tips are most likely caused by dry air from the heater running all day, which dries out the fern's foliage. [keyword: humid]
The tiny flies are most likely fungus gnats, whose larvae live in consistently wet potting soil and are not harming the plant much. [nothing harmful]

The white cottony spots are most likely mealybugs, a common sap-feeding pest on pothos, though the photo does not show them clearly and the pale patches could be natural variegation. Skip household products; rinse the leaves and wipe the pests off with soapy water. [nothing harmful]
